5-1.author: editorial source audit (agent), owner sign-off pending
5-1.rationale: Chapter 5 batch 04, re-checked 19 November 2026 against the RBI Digital Payments - E-mandate Framework, 2026 (RBI/DPSS/2026-27/396, 21 April 2026, https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13374), sections 6 and 8: pre-transaction notification at least 24 hours before the debit and an opt-out validated by AFA; AFA is required above Rs 15,000 per transaction, while insurance premiums, mutual-fund subscriptions and credit-card bill payments are exempt from AFA up to Rs 1,00,000 per transaction. The unconditional claim that a merchant cannot force a renewal after cancellation was softened to the issuer obligation; the Rs 1,00,000 exceptions were added.

5-4.author: editorial source audit (agent), owner sign-off pending
5-4.rationale: Chapter 5 batch 04, corrected 19 November 2026: the 7 May 2026 Fourth Amendment was only a draft. The final Telecom Consumers Complaint Redressal (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026 were issued on 2 November 2026 (PIB Release ID 2331704, https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2331704; TRAI regulation https://trai.gov.in/sites/default/files/2026-11/Regulation_02112026.pdf). Salient features: complaint centres round the clock with at least 16 hours of human assistance; complaints and appeals through the provider app, website and portal; appeal filing window cut from 30 to 15 days after disposal; appellate authority of regular management employees with 5 years experience deciding within 15 days; PwD desks and accessibility; feedback surveys, oversight committees, regulatory review and financial disincentives. The three-level route is retained. The notification commencement clause could not be read from the rendered PDF, so the tip tells readers to confirm commencement before relying on the 15-day window.
